How to read the numbers

cells.text: Hours logged divided by hours budgeted
At 80 percent in a phase, review scope with the principal
Under 14 with sets unfinished means add drafting time now
RFIs still Open on a project
More than three means schedule a coordination call with the contractor
Aim to return within the contract review period

text.text: Every phase ends with a decision the client has signed. Writing the exit check down stops scope creeping backward.

cells.text: Program, budget range and site facts agreed
Materials and systems chosen; cost check done
Set coordinated and checked against code
Final inspection and punch list closed

text.text: Moving a project forward
Confirm the exit check in the project page.
Change the phase on the project row.
Create the drawing sets for the next phase with due dates.
RFIs
Log it the day it arrives with the raised date and who must answer.
Answer within five working days; if it needs a consultant, tell the contractor the date you expect.
If the answer changes drawings, issue a sketch or revised sheet and note it in the RFI.
Close the RFI when the contractor confirms.
Submittals
Check against the specification section, not just the drawings.
Mark Approved only when nothing needs changing; otherwise Revise and resubmit with marked-up notes.
Keep a clear line between approval of product data and responsibility for means and methods.
A late answer costs the contractor money. They will remember it at final payment.
Logging time
Log hours the same day against a project, never against a client alone.
Use plain task names that the principal can read in a fee review.
Reading the numbers

cells.text: Check the remaining deliverables for the phase
Talk to the client about scope before more work

text.text: At each phase end
Compare hours logged with the hours budgeted for that phase.
Note why you were over or under in the project page.
Use the lesson when pricing the next project.
Before you go
Latest drawing set, RFI list and open submittals
Camera, tape, level, boots and safety gear
Contractor told the time and who is coming
On site
Walk the work against the drawings, area by area.
Photograph each area and name the file with the date and grid reference.
Write each issue as a sentence with a location and a number.
Afterwards
Send a field report within two working days.
Log new questions as RFIs.
Update the project's phase and hours.
